target_customer: Developers and teams building LLM apps and AI agents with a low code visual builder
problem: Building LangChain based LLM applications needed repetitive boilerplate code. Flowise gives a drag and drop canvas so developers and non developers can prototype and ship quickly.
business_model: Open source core with freemium cloud tiers (free to about 65 dollars a month) and enterprise self hosting
product_category: Open source low code AI agent and LLM app builder

founders.name: Henry Heng
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: cofounder of Flowise, ex software engineer at Fidelity Investments. Named CEO and co-founder in the Workday press release of 2025-08-14.

founders.name: Chung Yau Ong
founders.background_notes: YC page bio only says cofounder of Flowise.

technical_complexity.rationale: A node based UI wrapping LangChain.js components is standard web engineering. Keeping up with fast moving model and vector store integrations was the ongoing burden.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and built on LangChain, so rivals like Langflow offered a similar canvas. Community size and integrations gave some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing visual builders appeared, and Workday bought Flowise in August 2025 to give customers an agent builder for HR and finance.

market_need_then: LangChain grew very quickly in early 2023 and many developers wanted simpler ways to build chatbots and RAG apps, which created demand for visual builders.

branding.domain_note: Uses flowiseai.com. Origin of the domain not found.

identity.logo: white wordmark in the site header; no mascot description found
identity.visual_style: clean, screenshot driven, feature cards with some emoji accents
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, upbeat and developer oriented with headings like Iterate, fast.

branding.community_and_virality: Active Discord community, webinars and a podcast appearance, plus a large open source following per sources.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known in the open source LLM builder community with a Discord and webinars, but no evidence of a mascot, merch or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Flowise grew as an open source visual builder on the 2023 LangChain wave and gained a developer community with very little capital. Workday acquired it in August 2025 to add an agent builder for HR and finance customers, and the standalone product is now being sunset per the site.
notes: Funding search run: aggregators (Seedtable, CB Insights, VCBacked, Extruct) give about 500K total with Y Combinator and Eight Capital, labelled seed or pre-seed in 2023, but no company post, press release, SEC filing or investor page confirms it and it matches the standard YC deal, so no round is recorded. A 107M USD deal listing with unrelated founders looks misattributed and is ignored. The Workday press release dated 2025-08-14 states the acquisition is complete, no terms disclosed. The earlier note that Heng is a Workday director was unsourced and is removed. The Flowise blog post on the Workday deal returned 503 earlier. No competitor source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty. Site says Flowise is being sunset. Funding completeness pass: 500K round (2023) recorded from Seedtable as seed; VCBacked and Extruct label it pre-seed and name Eight Capital. Single database, likely the standard YC deal.
